statement: "Tonight" is a song by British singer and songwriter PinkPantheress.
It was released through Warner Records on 4 April 2025 as the lead single from her second mixtape, Fancy That (2025).
PinkPantheress wrote and produced the song with Aksel Arvid and Count Baldor.
Musically, "Tonight" is a dance, dance-pop, house, and bassline track that features synthesisers and four-on-the-floor beats.
It samples orchestral arrangements and strings from Panic! at the Disco's song "Do You Know What I'm Seeing?" from their album Pretty. Odd. (2008).
Panic! at the Disco's song "Do You Know What I'm Seeing?" was written by Brendon Urie, Ryan Ross, Spencer Smith, and Jon Walker.
In the lyrics, the song's narrator makes sexual advances towards her crush.
Music critics generally praised "Tonight" for its production and PinkPantheress's vocal performance.
Commercially, the track reached the national charts of Ireland and the United Kingdom.
The music video for "Tonight" was directed by Charlotte Rutherford.
The music video depicts PinkPantheress and her friends hosting a rowdy party at a manor house, where they kiss passionately and engage in pillow fights.
The period drama–inspired video contains various fashion and aesthetic choices that evoke the Regency era and the television series Bridgerton.
PinkPantheress included "Tonight" in the set list of her third concert tour, An Evening With... PinkPantheress (2025–2026).
PinkPantheress performed "Tonight" at several other events.
PinkPantheress released her debut mixtape, To Hell with It, on 15 October 2021.
PinkPantheress released her debut studio album, Heaven Knows, on 10 November 2023.
PinkPantheress revealed that she was working on new music in July 2024.
PinkPantheress cancelled her remaining 2024 concerts to focus on her health.
PinkPantheress tweeted images of herself in a studio in January 2025, writing, "Oh, we are soooo back! [...] Thanks for waiting on me".

In an interview with Mixmag in March 2025, PinkPantheress said that she had been writing about "letting expectations go" and "trying to strike a balance between being a pop star and also being experimental".
PinkPantheress released "Tonight" digitally on 4 April 2025 as the lead single from her second mixtape, Fancy That (2025).
Warner Records promoted the song to Italian radio airplay on 11 April 2025.
On 10 October 2025, a remix of "Tonight" featuring English singer Jade Thirlwall was released as part of Fancy That's remix edition Fancy Some More.
On 10 October 2025, two remixes by Basement Jaxx and Joe Goddard were released as part of Fancy That's remix edition Fancy Some More.
"Tonight" reached number 35 on the national charts of the United Kingdom.
"Tonight" reached number 88 on the national charts of Ireland.
In the United States, the track peaked at number 5 on the Hot Dance/Pop Songs chart.
In the United States, the track peaked at number 25 on the Bubbling Under Hot 100 Singles chart.
"Tonight" reached number 7 on the New Zealand Hot Singles chart.
"Tonight" reached number 12 on the Japan Hot Overseas chart.
"Tonight" reached number 65 on the Lithuania Airplay chart.
PinkPantheress engineered and programmed "Tonight" with Arvid.
Producer Phil provided additional production for "Tonight".
The song was mixed by Nickie Jon Pabón.
The song was mastered by Colin Leonard.
"Tonight" is 2 minutes and 54 seconds long.
Prior to its release, PinkPantheress wrote on social media, "Ion wanna see no more song length jokes after this song comes out on Friday".
PinkPantheress's social media post alluded to her songs usually being about 2 minutes and 30 seconds long.
"Tonight" is a synth-driven dance, dance-pop, house, and bassline track with four-on-the-floor beats, hyperpop vocals, and UK garage and drum and bass influences.
The song begins with orchestral strings before transitioning into its dance–heavy production.
Critics described the bass part of "Tonight" as "thumping", "hefty", "groovy", "wonky", and "bubbly".
In the lyrics, the song's narrator flirts with her shy crush.
The refrain of "Tonight" states: "You want sex with me? Huh? / Come talk to me, come on".
PinkPantheress stated that she wanted the narrator to be "the one in control", unlike her previous songs in which "the ball is in the other person's court".
Jon Pareles of The New York Times wrote that PinkPantheress's vocals on the track were "almost nonchalant".
Rolling Stone's Will Hermes believed that PinkPantheress was "plasticizing her voice".
Alexis Petridis of The Guardian thought that the lyrics of "Tonight" referenced the songs "Complicated" (2002) by Avril Lavigne and "Sex on Fire" (2008) by Kings of Leon.
Robin Murray of Clash dubbed "Tonight" a "ridiculously infectious [...] dose of pop futurism that arrives with a sly grin on its face".
Sal Cinquemani of Slant Magazine described "Tonight" as an "unabashed sex song".
Zachary Horvath from HotNewHipHop praised the song's overall sound.
Zachary Horvath from HotNewHipHop thought that "Tonight" exemplified PinkPantheress's "addicting" production style and "wildly entrancing" vocal delivery.
NME's Kyann-Sian Williams commended "Tonight"'s adrenaline-pumping atmosphere.
Pitchfork's Harry Tafoya deemed the track "impressive".
Pitchfork's Harry Tafoya lauded how "the fast-paced thump mirrors a dawning sense of romantic urgency" in "Tonight".
Elaina Bernstein from Hypebeast selected "Tonight" as one of the best songs of its release week.
Derrick Rossignol from Uproxx selected "Tonight" as one of the best songs of its release week.
The editorial staff of Consequence selected "Tonight" as one of the best songs of its release week.
Consequence praised PinkPantheress's "feathery" vocals on "Tonight".
Consequence praised the combination of baroque strings with club–driven beats in "Tonight".
Billboard listed "Tonight" as one of their "R&B/Hip-Hop Fresh Picks of the Week".
Michael Saponara lauded "Tonight"'s production and mature narrative.
Wonderland similarly lauded "Tonight"'s production and "playful" lyrics.
Wonderland included "Tonight" on their list of the best newly released songs.
In June 2025, "Tonight" was picked as one of the best songs of the year by Billboard, ranking 20 out of 50.
In June 2025, "Tonight" was picked as one of the best songs of the year by Consequence, ranking 24 out of 100.
Paolo Ragusa from Consequence commended PinkPantheress's "honeyed vocals and untouchable attitude" on "Tonight".
Paolo Ragusa from Consequence commended "Tonight"'s "roomy, nostalgic production".
Paolo Ragusa from Consequence thought that the track "Tonight" was "relatively straightforward" overall.
Publications such as NME, Vogue, Cosmopolitan, and Exclaim! picked "Tonight" as one of the "songs of the summer".
Vogue's Liam Hess deemed "Tonight" the highlight of Fancy That.
Vogue's Liam Hess described "Tonight" as a "three-minute slice of pop perfection".
Vogue's Liam Hess praised "Tonight"'s composition and catchy refrain.
NME's Karen Gwee described "Tonight" as "light and addictive".
Cosmopolitan's Samantha Olson stated that "Tonight" "makes a Panic! at the Disco sample sound like a voguing track made for endless nights breaking a sweat on the dance floor".
Maria Sherman from the Associated Press picked "Tonight" as the "song of the summer for the chronically online".
The music video for "Tonight", directed by Charlotte Rutherford, was released on 4 April 2025, the same day as the song's release.

PinkPantheress stated that she wanted to make a "more classic pop video, where you have sets and you have a different hairstyle than usual and a dress that looks like something you wouldn't wear" for "Tonight".
The music video for "Tonight" depicts PinkPantheress and her friends riding on bicycles and carriages to a manor house.
In the music video for "Tonight", PinkPantheress and her friends throw a chaotic party.
In the music video for "Tonight", PinkPantheress and her friends kiss passionately.
In the music video for "Tonight", PinkPantheress and her friends engage in pillow fights.
At the party in the music video for "Tonight", a DJ spins records on a phonograph.
At the party in the music video for "Tonight", a woman's hair sets on fire.
At the party in the music video for "Tonight", a man inside of a portrait steps out of it.
The costumes in the period drama–inspired video for "Tonight" incorporate corsets, powdered wigs, and pearls.
Media publications described the costumes in the "Tonight" music video as reminiscent of the Regency era and the television series Bridgerton.
PinkPantheress revealed that the music video for "Tonight" was inspired by Bridgerton.
PinkPantheress revealed that the music video for "Tonight" was inspired by the music video for Jamiroquai's song "King for a Day" (1999).
The music video for Jamiroquai's song "King for a Day" (1999) showcases elements from the Georgian era.
The dance that PinkPantheress performed in the music video for "Tonight" went viral on the online video platform TikTok.
The dance went viral following PinkPantheress's dance challenges with other celebrities, including American rapper Doechii.
PinkPantheress performed "Tonight" at the Glastonbury Festival on 27 June 2025.
On 30 July 2025, PinkPantheress sang "Tonight" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon as part of a medley with the Fancy That tracks "Illegal" and "Girl Like Me".
PinkPantheress was accompanied by a DJ and several backup dancers during her performance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.
PinkPantheress played a stripped-down version of "Tonight" on NPR's Tiny Desk Concerts in September 2025.
PinkPantheress was joined by a backup band for her performance of "Tonight" on NPR's Tiny Desk Concerts.
On 8 October 2025, PinkPantheress performed the track "Tonight" on BBC Radio 1's Live Lounge.
PinkPantheress included "Tonight" in the set list of her third concert tour, An Evening With... PinkPantheress (2025–2026).
PinkPantheress's third concert tour, An Evening With... PinkPantheress (2025–2026), included shows in the UK and North America.
PinkPantheress was accompanied by two dancers dubbed "the Pinkettes" during her third concert tour.
Credits for "Tonight" are adapted from Qobuz.
"Tonight" reached a peak position of 88 on the Ireland (IRMA) chart in 2025.
"Tonight" reached a peak position of 12 on the Japan Hot Overseas (Billboard Japan) chart in 2025.
"Tonight" reached a peak position of 65 on the Lithuania Airplay (TopHit) chart in 2025.
"Tonight" reached a peak position of 7 on the New Zealand Hot Singles (RMNZ) chart in 2025.
